body.q: A business buys a machine for $50 000. It expects to use it for 5 years and then sell it for $5 000. Using the straight-line method, what is the annual depreciation charge?
body.why: Straight-line depreciation = (cost - residual value) / useful life = ($50 000 - $5 000) / 5 = $9 000.

body.q: A vehicle cost $20 000 and is depreciated at 25% per year using the reducing balance method. What is the depreciation charge for the second year?
body.why: Year 1 charge is $5 000, leaving a net book value of $15 000, so year 2 charge is 25% of $15 000 = $3 750.

o: To spread the cost of the asset over its useful life
To set aside cash to replace the asset
To show the current market value of the asset
To reduce the amount of tax paid on sales
body.q: Which of the following is the main reason a business charges depreciation on a non-current asset?
body.why: Depreciation applies the matching concept by allocating the asset's cost to the periods that benefit from its use.

o: Debit depreciation expense; credit provision for depreciation
Debit provision for depreciation; credit depreciation expense
Debit bank; credit provision for depreciation
body.q: What is the correct double entry to record the annual depreciation charge on equipment?
body.why: Depreciation is an expense (debit) and the accumulated amount is built up in the provision for depreciation account (credit).

body.q: A business has equipment with a cost of $12 000 and a provision for depreciation of $7 500. What is the net book value of the equipment?
body.why: Net book value = cost - accumulated depreciation = $12 000 - $7 500 = $4 500.

body.q: Which of the following is NOT a factor that causes non-current assets to depreciate?
body.why: Owner's capital does not affect an asset's physical or economic decline, whereas wear and tear, obsolescence and time do.

body.q: A machine was bought for $8 000 and depreciated for 3 years at $1 500 per year. It is then sold for $3 900. What is the result of the disposal?
body.why: Net book value is $8 000 - $4 500 = $3 500; selling for $3 900 gives a profit of $400, so the correct answer is actually a profit of $400.

o: In the income statement as an expense
In the statement of financial position as a current liability
In the income statement as part of cost of sales only
In the statement of financial position as a current asset
body.q: Where does the depreciation expense for the year appear in the final accounts of a sole trader?
body.why: Depreciation is an expense of the year and is deducted in the income statement, reducing profit.

body.q: Which accounting concept is being applied when a business uses the same depreciation method from year to year?
body.why: The consistency concept requires the same accounting methods to be applied from one period to the next so results are comparable.

body.q: A business buys a computer for $2 400 with no residual value and an expected life of 4 years. After 2 years it is still in use. What is the net book value at the end of year 2 using straight-line depreciation?
body.why: Annual depreciation is $2 400 / 4 = $600, so after 2 years accumulated depreciation is $1 200 and net book value is $2 400 - $1 200 = $1 200.
